title: BTEC First Certificate in Engineering — selected Unit 8

handoff.scope: Inventory and generation/extraction requirements only. No symbol geometry, device models, footprints or application subfolder feature is implemented.
handoff.folder_semantics: folder is a proposed slash-separated logical path, not a claim of support in the current TinyCAD library browser.
handoff.source_document_base: All source_document paths are relative to the repository root, including in standalone library files.
handoff.identity: id is stable within a library; extraction may deduplicate by canonical_symbol_id, but each library is complete and permits independent duplicate assets.
handoff.pin_contract: Logical terminal numbers and signal names are not physical package pinouts. Resolve real package pins from an authoritative device reference before generating package-specific symbols.
handoff.conventions: Prefer IEC/UK teaching symbols. Power pins and polarity should remain explicit. Built-in instruments, probes, independent waveform sources and voltage-controlled sources are excluded from symbol generation. Use existing_tools configuration with the native tool defaults.
handoff.existing_tools: existing_tools and existing_tool_ids refer to supplied non-library tools, not generation requirements. Never recreate these as library symbols.
handoff.inventory_not_bom: One record per reusable symbol type, not per component instance. A bridge can be assembled from repeated diode/resistor symbols. Different resistance/capacitance values are properties, not separate symbols.
handoff.model_warning: Every record is marked not ready to simulate from this manifest. A successful extraction of artwork does not establish a valid model, mapping or instrument implementation.
handoff.optionality: experiment_symbol_ids are a coverage set of proposed implementations and comparisons, not a minimal mandatory BOM; common support symbols and explicitly optional additions are separately identified.

experiments.title: Resistor combinations
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare series and parallel loads, predict supply current, and verify voltage sharing. Save a calculation alongside the circuit and numerical readings.

experiments.title: Adjustable sensor input
experiments.catalogue_description: Use a fixed resistor and variable sensor-equivalent resistance. Compare divider output over measured light or temperature conditions. The entered resistance is an assumption, not an optical or thermal simulation.

experiments.title: Push-button input and pull resistor
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw push-to-make and push-to-break arrangements. Use an explicit switch model or separate open/closed circuits to test the resulting input voltage.

experiments.title: LED output and current limiting
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare several limiting resistors and supplies using an LED model. Record current and resistor power; do not equate simulated current with measured brightness.

experiments.title: BJT switching stage
experiments.catalogue_description: Sweep the input to an NPN or PNP stage driving an electrical load. Compare input, output and device currents. Supply the correct model and pin mapping.

experiments.title: Darlington input stage
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare a single transistor with a pair for the same load. Investigate the input drive needed to reach a stated output condition.

experiments.title: FET switching stage
experiments.catalogue_description: Apply a gate-voltage sweep or pulse. Compare off/on output and load current using a chosen FET model.

experiments.title: Thyristor latch
experiments.catalogue_description: Apply a gate pulse and observe whether conduction persists after it ends. Model interruption of load current to reset the device. A transistor model is not an SCR substitute.

experiments.title: Threshold alarm
experiments.catalogue_description: Combine a sensor-equivalent input, comparator/transistor and LED load. Set a target threshold and compare predicted switching with measured sensor values. This is one possible implementation of the unit's design work.

experiments.title: RC timing stage
experiments.catalogue_description: Capture capacitor voltage after a source step. Change R and C separately and compare the measured delay to a chosen threshold.

experiments.title: Timer in monostable mode
experiments.catalogue_description: Use a compatible timer model, trigger once and measure pulse duration. Change the timing components. A predefined pulse source cannot demonstrate the timer's timing law.

experiments.title: Timer in astable mode
experiments.catalogue_description: Capture a timer's output and compare frequency/duty cycle for different component values. A flashing LED's electrical drive can be tested without modelling visual flashing.

experiments.title: Inductive-output protection
experiments.catalogue_description: Represent a relay coil by an explicit electrical model and compare switch-node voltage with and without a protection diode. Mechanical operation is outside the model.

experiments.title: Power-source suitability
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare the same circuit with an ideal source and a source having stated internal resistance. Battery chemistry and solar illumination need separate models or measurements.

experiments.title: PIC-based counter and display connections
experiments.catalogue_description: Document input switch, controller pins, supplies and display connections. Firmware execution, flowchart programming and seven-segment decoding are not ready-made TinyCAD workflows. Electrical interface stages can be tested separately.

experiments.title: Test-point and fault-diagnosis exercise
experiments.catalogue_description: Prepare a correct circuit and separate manually edited open/short/wrong-value versions. Predict diagnostic voltage/current readings. Record a test sequence for checking the physical build; this does not rely on an automatic fault-injection feature.

experiments.title: Construction and soldering preparation
experiments.catalogue_description: Produce a labelled schematic, polarity notes and a connectivity checklist for the physical assembly. TinyCAD does not turn the schematic into a breadboard photograph, demonstrate soldering competence or inspect joints.
